text:
ravi: Quick pre-read for tomorrow's design review 1: new direction idea for pinned models in the compare table. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/newflow/pinned-breadcrumbs

zoe: Saw the link. What's the core difference vs the current inline pin?

ravi: Instead of an icon inside each row, show a compact breadcrumb strip above the table listing pinned models with tiny perf badges and a close (unpin) control. Keeps rows ultra-clean and preserves context when collapsed.

marco: I like the low-clutter angle. Two practical concerns: discoverability (users may not realize the breadcrumb exists) and keyboard access. We should surface a modest animation when the first pin appears and ensure the breadcrumb is tabbable as a region.

anya: Accessibility checklist: breadcrumb strip needs role="region" and aria-label="Pinned models"; each crumb should be a button with aria-pressed. Perf badges in crumbs must still meet contrast. Also provide sr-only text for the badge values (e.g., "Latency 23ms, Cost $0.002 per 1k"). That helps screen readers without cluttering the UI.

marco: Alternative to breadcrumb: reuse the existing selection/checkbox column. Add a secondary micro-affordance (star) next to the checkbox so pinning sits in one column, avoiding new header elements. The star stays visible when rows collapse because it's colocated with the selection affordance.

zoe: Checkbox-column star is neat and probably easier for power users who already look there, but we need to keep hit-targets large enough (44px) and avoid overlapping selection behaviour. Also for RTL we must use logical CSS so the star flips correctly.

ravi: Good point on RTL. We'll test both patterns with i18n samples.

anya: Microcopy: change tooltip from "Pin version" to "Keep this model visible in compare". Toast copy when a pin is hidden by filters: "Pinned model hidden by filters. Show pinned models? [Show]". Also ensure tooltip content is keyboard-triggerable (focus + enter) not only hover.

marco: Implementation note: if we add a star into the checkbox column, do it as an absolutely-positioned element within the cell to avoid changing column width. Expand the cell's focusable area via padding or an invisible hitbox so it's still reachable on touch.

ravi: Analytics: capture pin.created, pin.toggled, pin.shown (breadcrumb|inline-star), pin.revealed-by-filter. We'll want time-to-discover metrics for breadcrumb vs inline-star tests.

qa-bot: Created ticket UX-7033: "Compare: breadcrumb vs inline-star pin patterns + accessibility + i18n checks" and attached Figma frames.

product-ops: Added ACs: 1) breadcrumb region is tabbable and labelled; 2) star in checkbox column is keyboard focusable and pressable via Space/Enter; 3) perf badges meet 4.5:1 contrast or have sr-only fallback; 4) RTL & localization overflow handled; 5) analytics events emitted. Assigned to eng-frontend and ux-research.

zoe: Can we prototype both and run a quick five-person unmoderated task test? I want to see how fast people pin and find pinned items.

ravi: Yes, I'll spin up two quick prototypes (breadcrumb strip + checkbox-star) and drop them in the review. Will include keyboard flows, RTL sample, and the copy variations. Demo tomorrow morning.
